findings.title: Negative delay causes sleep to raise ValueError, masking the original exception
findings.body: If `delay` is negative, `sleep(delay)` raises `ValueError: sleep length must be non-negative`. This error is raised inside the `except` block but outside the `try` block, so it propagates out of `retry` immediately, masking the original exception from `operation()`. The caller receives a `ValueError` about sleep length instead of the actual error from their operation. A validation check for `delay < 0` should raise a clear `ValueError` before the loop starts, or the sleep call should be guarded. The current behavior makes debugging harder when a negative delay is accidentally passed.

findings.title: isoformat() can produce negative year strings, contrary to docstring intent
findings.body: The docstring states the function rejects years outside 1..9999 and claims '{year:04d}' alone would emit "-001" or "10000". The implementation passes the raw year into datetime.date, which raises ValueError for year<1 or year>9999, so those are rejected. However, if the caller later relies on the returned string for years exactly at the boundary or for years that are valid but non-positive (which datetime forbids), the note is misleading. More importantly, datetime.date.isoformat() for year < 1000 does not zero-pad to four digits (e.g., year 9 yields "9-01-01", not "0009-01-01"), so the "YYYY" guarantee in the docstring is not actually provided for years 1-999. This is a minor correctness/maintainability issue introduced by the new module.
